stem: Regarding the inheritance of bleeding disorders, how does Hemophilia A and B typically differ from von Willebrand disease?

options.text: Hemophilia is autosomal dominant, while von Willebrand is X-linked.
Hemophilia is X-linked, whereas von Willebrand is usually autosomal dominant.
Both are X-linked, but von Willebrand only affects females.
Hemophilia is an acquired condition, whereas von Willebrand is always genetic.

explanation: Hemophilia A and B affect males through X-linked inheritance, while von Willebrand disease affects both males and females across generations.
rationale: Recall which disorder specifically affects males in the family history.

optionExplanations.A: This reverses the actual inheritance patterns described in the lecture.
optionExplanations.B: Hemophilia A and B affect males through X-linked inheritance, while von Willebrand disease affects both males and females across generations.
optionExplanations.C: Von Willebrand disease is autosomal, meaning it is not linked to the sex chromosomes.
optionExplanations.D: Both conditions are described as genetic factor deficiencies.
